title: Sectors Brace for Trade War
text:
Photo: Getty Images 
Here we go, folks. President Trump is planning to slap tariffs on up to $50 billion of Chinese imports, and China is vowing to respond .
My Barron’s colleague Reshma Kapadia notes that “some see the move as bad news for several large U.S. agricultural and consumer companies.” China is the biggest buyer of U.S. soybeans, and it could hurt companies like Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) and farm-equipment maker Deere (DE), David Riedel, with Riedel Research, writes. 
“China could also retaliate by making its much sought-after consumers harder to reach by U.S. companies, which have staked much of their growth on emerging market consumers,” Kapadia writes. Companies like Nike (NKE), Apple (AAPL), Yum! Brands (YUM), and Starbucks (SBUX) could find it harder to reach the Chinese market. Energy, tech and materials could also be hit. 
That said, the complex global value chain makes predictions somewhat tricky. 
Meanwhile, Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley FBR, tells CNBC the equity markets “have not parsed the potential for a trade war . The two policies we’re concerned about are monetary policy and trade policy, and trade policy is coming at us like a freight train right now. The outcome of this could be dangerous.” 
Advisors, what are you telling your clients about today’s news? E-mail us at advisor.editors@barrons.com . 
--Steve Garmhausen
